p.src: Now Song Jiang, having taken Dongping Prefecture, withdrew his army to Anshan Town and was preparing to return to the stronghold when Bai Sheng came to report: “Lu Junyi went to attack Dongchang Prefecture and has lost two battles in succession. Within the city is a fierce general surnamed Zhang and named Qing. He is a native of Zhangde Prefecture and began his career in the Tiger Cavalry. He is skilled at striking men with flying stones, and never misses; people call him ‘the Featherless Arrow.’ He has two lieutenants under him. One is Gong Wang, called ‘Flower-Necked Tiger’; his whole body is tattooed with tiger stripes, a tiger’s head is tattooed across his neck, and he can cast javelins from horseback. The other is Ding Desun, called ‘Arrow-Struck Tiger’; scars cover his cheeks and neck, and he can cast forked spears from horseback. When Squire Lu led his troops to the border, the enemy refused battle for ten days straight. The day before yesterday, Zhang Qing came out of the city to engage us, and Hao Siwen rode forth to meet him. After they had fought many bouts, Zhang Qing turned and fled. Hao Siwen pursued him, but a stone struck him at the corner of the forehead and knocked him from his horse. But Yan Qing shot a crossbow bolt into Zhang Qing’s warhorse. Thus Hao Siwen’s life was saved, though we lost the battle. The next day, Fan Rui the ‘Demon King of Chaos’ led Xiang Chong and Li Gun out with their shields whirling, but unexpectedly Ding Desun cast a marked fork from beneath his arm and struck Xiang Chong squarely; so we lost another battle. Both men are now recuperating aboard a boat. The strategist specially ordered me to ask you, elder brother, to hurry to our aid.” When Song Jiang heard this, he sighed: “Lu Junyi truly has no luck at all! I expressly sent Scholar Wu and Gongsun Sheng to assist him, hoping only that he would win glory in battle and gain some standing in the stronghold. Who would have thought he would meet another worthy foe! Since matters stand thus, all of us brothers shall take our troops to his aid.” He immediately issued the order, and the whole army set out. The generals mounted and followed Song Jiang all the way to the borders of Dongchang. Lu Junyi and the others came to receive them and related all that had happened; for the time being, they made camp.

p.src: While they were still deliberating, a soldier reported that Zhang Qing, the ‘Featherless Arrow,’ had come to challenge them. Song Jiang at once led his men out and arrayed his forces on an open plain. Every chief, great and small, mounted and gathered beneath the commander’s banner. Looking across from horseback, Song Jiang saw the opposing ranks drawn in a single line, their banners divided among five colors. When the drums had sounded three times, Zhang Qing, the ‘Featherless Arrow,’ rode forth. How was he arrayed? A lyric in the tune ‘Water Melody’ praises Zhang Qing’s valor: A madder-red tassel glimmers beneath his headcloth; wolf-slender waist and ape-long arms frame his stalwart form. Brocade clothes and an embroidered jacket; beneath his robe, a glimpse of deepest blue. Sitting aslant in his carved saddle, he lightly urges on a blue roan with a jade bridle. Sunflower-shaped precious stirrups set the burnished brass bells ringing. Pheasant plumes trail behind as the four fleet hooves fly. Golden rings sway, while crimson tassels flutter from the jade serpent. Stones from his brocade pouch fly lightly as shooting stars. He needs no mighty bow or rigid crossbow, no pellet bow or flying bell; wherever his missile strikes, a life must fall. Dongchang’s mounted general—Zhang Qing, the ‘Featherless Arrow.’

p.src: Song Jiang asked, “Who will go and fight Zhang Qing?” At his side, one hero was provoked; in fury he spurred his horse, brandished his hooked spear, and rode before the lines. Song Jiang looked and saw that it was Xu Ning, the Gold-Lance Hand. Song Jiang was secretly delighted and said, “This man is indeed a match for him.” Xu Ning galloped straight at Zhang Qing. The two horses met, and both spears rose together. Before five bouts had passed, Zhang Qing turned and fled. Xu Ning gave chase. Zhang Qing feigned with the long spear in his left hand, reached into his brocade pouch with his right, drew out a stone, and twisted around. Seeing Xu Ning’s face close at hand, he loosed the stone. Alas for that fierce and valiant hero—the stone struck him between the brows, and he pitched from his horse. Gong Wang and Ding Desun rushed forward to seize him. But Song Jiang had many men in his ranks; Lü Fang and Guo Sheng promptly rode out, each wielding a halberd, and rescued him back to their lines. Song Jiang and the others were greatly shocked, and all lost color. He asked again, “Which chief will take up the fight?” Before Song Jiang had finished speaking, a general shot out from behind his horse. It was Yan Shun, the ‘Brocade-Furred Tiger.’ Song Jiang was about to stop him, but the rider was already gone. Yan Shun engaged Zhang Qing and fought him for many bouts, but could not withstand him; he wheeled his horse and fled. Zhang Qing pursued him, took out a stone, and hurled it at Yan Shun’s back. It struck the protective mirror on his armor with a clang, and Yan Shun bent low over his saddle and escaped. A man in Song Jiang’s ranks cried out, “Why should we fear this wretch?” He spurred his horse, raised his lance, and shot out from the formation. Song Jiang looked and saw that it was Han Tao, the ‘Ever-Victorious General.’ Without exchanging words, he attacked Zhang Qing. As soon as their horses met, shouts thundered all around. Eager to display his skill before Song Jiang, Han Tao summoned all his spirit and fought Zhang Qing fiercely. Before ten bouts had passed, Zhang Qing fled. Han Tao suspected that he would cast a stone and did not pursue. Zhang Qing looked back and, seeing no pursuit, wheeled around and reined in his horse. Just as Han Tao leveled his lance to meet him, Zhang Qing brought out a concealed stone and struck him squarely in the hollow of the nose. Blood gushed forth, and Han Tao fled back to his own lines. Peng Qi flew into a rage at the sight. Without waiting for Song Gongming’s order, he brandished his three-pointed, double-edged blade and galloped straight at Zhang Qing. Before their horses had even met, Zhang Qing brought up the stone hidden in his hand and struck Peng Qi squarely on the cheek. Peng Qi dropped his three-pointed, double-edged blade and galloped back to the formation.

p.src: Seeing several of his generals defeated, Song Jiang grew alarmed and was about to withdraw his forces. But then a man behind Lu Junyi cried out, “If our martial renown is broken today, how shall we fight tomorrow? Let us see whether his stones can strike me!” Song Jiang looked and saw Xuan Zan, the ‘Ugly Prince-Consort,’ spur his horse, whirl his saber, and charge straight at Zhang Qing. Zhang Qing said, “One comes, one flees; two come, two run away. Do you know the skill of my flying stones?” Xuan Zan replied, “You may strike others, but how could you touch me?” Before he had finished speaking, Zhang Qing raised his hand and struck Xuan Zan squarely beside the mouth with a stone, toppling him from his horse. Gong Wang and Ding Desun were about to seize him, but Song Jiang’s ranks were too numerous, and his generals rescued him back to their formation. At this, Song Jiang’s fury soared to the heavens. Drawing his sword, he cut his robe and swore: “If I do not capture this man, I swear I shall not withdraw my army!” Seeing Song Jiang swear this oath, Huyan Zhuo said, “Elder brother, if you speak so, what use are we brothers to you?” He spurred his black horse, Kicking Snow, and rode straight before the lines, cursing Zhang Qing: “You pampered brat, relying on your paltry strength and courage! Do you know the great general Huyan Zhuo?” Zhang Qing replied, “You are a defeated general who disgraced the realm; you too shall suffer at my hands!” Before the words had ended, a stone came flying. Seeing the stone fly toward him, Huyan Zhuo hurriedly raised his whip to block it, but it struck his wrist. After that single blow he could no longer wield his steel whip and returned to his own lines.

p.src: Song Jiang said, “All our cavalry commanders have been wounded. Which infantry commander dares capture this Zhang Qing?” Then Liu Tang emerged from the ranks, gripping his broad-bladed sword and boldly advancing to fight. At the sight of him, Zhang Qing laughed and cursed, “You defeated wretch! Even the cavalry lost to me—what hope has a foot soldier?” Liu Tang flew into a rage and charged straight at Zhang Qing. Zhang Qing declined to engage and galloped back toward his lines. Liu Tang pursued him, and man and horse met head-on. Quick of hand, Liu Tang slashed with his broad-bladed sword and struck Zhang Qing’s warhorse. The horse kicked up its hind legs, and its tail lashed Liu Tang across the face. His vision bursting into stars, he was promptly felled by a single stone from Zhang Qing. Just as he struggled to rise, soldiers rushed from the formation, seized him by the arms and legs, and dragged him inside. Song Jiang shouted, “Who will go and rescue Liu Tang?” At once Yang Zhi, the Blue-Faced Beast, spurred his horse, brandished his saber, and charged straight at Zhang Qing. Zhang Qing feinted with his spear. Yang Zhi slashed at him, but Zhang Qing ducked low in the stirrups, and the blade cut only empty air. Zhang Qing took a stone in hand and cried, “Take this!” The stone flew past beneath Yang Zhi’s ribs. Zhang Qing hurled another stone. It struck Yang Zhi’s helmet with a clang, frightening him out of his wits, and he bent low over his saddle and fled back to his lines. Seeing this, Song Jiang brooded anxiously, “If our fighting spirit is broken today, how can we return to Liangshan Marsh? Who will avenge this humiliation for me?”

p.src: Hearing this, Zhu Tong looked at Lei Heng and said, “One man is no match for him. Let the two of us attack from both sides.” Zhu Tong took the left and Lei Heng the right, and the two charged from the formation with their broad-bladed swords. Zhang Qing laughed. “One was useless, so now you add another! Come even ten at a time—what difference would it make?” Showing no fear whatsoever, he concealed two stones in his hands as he sat his horse. Lei Heng arrived first. Zhang Qing raised his hand with the force of the Treasure-Summoning Seventh Youth. As the stone came flying, how could Lei Heng evade it with his face exposed? Before he could lift his head to look, the stone struck his forehead, and he toppled heavily to the ground. Zhu Tong hurried forward to rescue him, but another stone struck him on the neck. Guan Sheng saw them wounded from the formation. Summoning his tremendous might, he swung up his Green Dragon Saber, urged on his Red Hare, and came to rescue Zhu Tong and Lei Heng. He had just snatched the two men away and was hastening back to the lines when Zhang Qing hurled another stone. Guan Sheng swiftly blocked it with his saber; it struck the edge squarely and sent sparks flying. Guan Sheng had no desire to prolong the fight and reined in his horse to withdraw.

p.src: Dong Ping, the Double-Speared General, saw this and thought, “I have only just submitted to Song Jiang. The two spears crossed and clashed over the field, while their four arms whirled in furious confusion. After some five or seven bouts, Zhang Qing wheeled his horse and fled. Dong Ping cried, “Others may fall to your stones, but how could they ever touch me?” Zhang Qing steadied his spear shaft and drew a stone from his brocade pouch. When his hand rose, it was truly like a shooting star flashing with lightning; the hurtling stone might have made ghosts wail and gods start in terror. Sharp-eyed and quick-handed, Dong Ping knocked the stone aside. Seeing that he had missed, Zhang Qing took a second stone and hurled it. Dong Ping dodged that one as well. After both stones missed, Zhang Qing began to panic. Their horses raced nose to tail. When Zhang Qing reached the left side of the entrance to his lines, Dong Ping thrust a spear at his back. Zhang Qing swerved and ducked low in the stirrups, so Dong Ping’s thrust missed. The spear drove past, and Dong Ping’s horse drew abreast of Zhang Qing’s. Zhang Qing cast aside his spear and seized Dong Ping, spear and arm together, with both hands. He gave a mighty tug but could not pull him over, and the two grappled in a tangled mass.

With a sharp sound it struck Ding Desun’s horse squarely in the hoof. The horse fell, and Lü Fang and Guo Sheng seized Ding Desun and brought him across to their lines. Zhang Qing wanted to rescue him, but he was too heavily outnumbered. He had no choice but to take Liu Tang and withdraw for the time being to Dongchang Prefecture. From the city wall, the prefect had seen Zhang Qing strike down fifteen of Liangshan Marsh’s great commanders one after another. Although Gong Wang and Ding Desun had been lost, they had also captured Liu Tang. After returning to the prefectural yamen, they first placed Liu Tang in a long cangue and sent him to prison, then met to discuss their next move.

On the other side, Ding Desun whirled his flying fork and fought Lü Fang and Guo Sheng for his life. He did not notice Yan Qing, the Prodigal, watching from within the entrance to the formation and thinking, “In a mere moment he has struck down fifteen of our great commanders. If we cannot even capture one of his lieutenants, how can we show our faces?”

Yan Qing laid down his staff, drew a crossbow from his side, set it to the string, and loosed a bolt. With a sharp sound it struck Ding Desun’s horse squarely in the hoof. The horse fell, and Lü Fang and Guo Sheng seized Ding Desun and brought him across to their lines.
Zhang Qing wanted to rescue him, but he was too heavily outnumbered. He had no choice but to take Liu Tang and withdraw for the time being to Dongchang Prefecture.

p.src: That night the moon shone faintly, and the sky was filled with stars. Before they had gone ten li, they saw a cluster of carts, and upon their banners was plainly written: “Provisions of Loyalty and Righteousness, Stronghold of the Marshes.” Zhang Qing looked and saw Lu Zhishen at the very front, carrying his Chan staff on his shoulder, his monk’s robe hitched up tightly. Zhang Qing said, “I will plant a stone on that bald donkey’s head.” Lu Zhishen, carrying his Chan staff, had already seen him, but pretended not to know and strode onward, forgetting to guard against his stones. As he walked, Zhang Qing shouted from horseback, “Take this!” A stone flew squarely into Lu Zhishen’s head. Blood gushed forth, and he toppled backward. Zhang Qing’s troops raised a united battle cry and rushed forward. Wu Song hastily brandished his pair of戒刀 and fought desperately to rescue Lu Zhishen, then abandoned the grain carts and fled. Zhang Qing seized the grain carts and, seeing that they indeed contained rice, rejoiced. He did not pursue Lu Zhishen but escorted the carts back into the city. The prefect was delighted at the sight and personally took charge of them. Zhang Qing said, “Now we shall seize the rice boats on the river.” The prefect said, “General, watch carefully for your opportunity.”

p.src: Zhang Qing mounted his horse and went around by the south gate. He could now see countless grain boats in the river harbor. Zhang Qing ordered the city gate opened, and they charged toward the river with a mighty shout. All at once dark clouds spread everywhere and black mist veiled the sky; when the cavalry and infantry looked back, no man could see the comrade before his face. This was Gongsun Sheng working his Daoist magic. At the sight, Zhang Qing’s heart panicked and his vision dimmed. He was about to turn back, but there was no way forward or back. Shouts rose chaotically on every side, and he could not tell whence the soldiers were coming. Lin Chong led the armored cavalry against him and drove Zhang Qing, horse and all, into the water. Waiting in the river, drawn up in a single line, were the eight naval chieftains: Li Jun, Zhang Heng, Zhang Shun, the three Ruan brothers, and the two Tong brothers. Even had Zhang Qing possessed three heads and six arms, how could he have struggled free? The three Ruan brothers seized him, bound him fast with cords and ropes, and delivered him into the stronghold. The naval chieftains hastened to report to Song Jiang, and Wu Yong at once urged all the chieftains, great and small, to attack the city through the night.

p.src: How could the prefect hold out alone? Hearing cannon fire on every side outside the walls and seeing the city gates opened, he was so terrified that he had nowhere to flee. Song Jiang’s forces stormed into the city and first rescued Liu Tang; then they opened the storehouses, sending one share of the money and grain to Liangshan Marsh and distributing another among the inhabitants. Because the prefect had always been honest and incorruptible, they spared his life.

p.src: Song Jiang and the others gathered in the prefectural yamen to meet together, when the naval chieftains brought Zhang Qing in under guard. Many of the brothers had been wounded by him and, grinding their teeth in fury, all came forward wanting to kill Zhang Qing. When Song Jiang saw him brought in, he personally descended the hall steps to welcome him and said apologetically, “We mistakenly offended your tigerish might; pray do not take it to heart.” He invited him up into the hall. Before he had finished speaking, Lu Zhishen appeared below the steps with a handkerchief wrapped around his head and his iron Chan staff in hand, charging straight at Zhang Qing to strike him. Song Jiang barred his way and repeatedly shouted him back: “How could I let you lay hands on him?” Seeing Song Jiang’s righteousness, Zhang Qing bowed his head to the floor and submitted. Song Jiang poured wine upon the earth and broke an arrow in oath: “If any of you brothers still seek vengeance in this fashion, may Heaven withhold its protection from me and let me die beneath sword and blade.” On hearing this, none dared say another word. Indeed, the Stars of the Heavenly Spirits were destined to assemble, and so their devotion naturally answered one another. When Song Jiang had finished his oath, he said, “Brothers, you must not harbor resentment.” Everyone laughed and was filled with joy. They made the troops ready, intending to return to the mountain stronghold.

p.src: Then, before Song Gongming, Zhang Qing recommended a veterinary physician of Dongchang Prefecture, whose compound surname was Huangfu and personal name was Duan. “This man is skilled at judging horses. He understands every ailment caused by heat or cold in livestock, and whether he administers medicine or uses needles, there is none he cannot cure. He truly possesses the talent of Bo Le! He is originally a native of Youzhou. Because he has blue-green eyes and a yellow beard, resembling a man of the western tribes, he is known as ‘Count Purple Beard.’ Liangshan Marsh has need of such a man. We may summon him to bring his wife and children and ascend the mountain with us.” Song Jiang was overjoyed to hear this: “If Huangfu Duan is willing to join us, it would delight me greatly.” Seeing how warmly Song Jiang regarded him, Zhang Qing immediately went and summoned the veterinary physician Huangfu Duan, who came to pay his respects to Song Jiang and all the chieftains. There is an old-style heptasyllabic poem devoted solely to Huangfu Duan’s medical art: His family-taught art has no rival under heaven; in tending noble steeds, these many years, his powers have seemed divine. His wondrous power to revive the dead and restore life defies all telling; how many more benefits he brings by saving the exhausted and supporting those in peril! All men praise Duke E’s black steed; Duke Guo’s green-eared courser came from the Wowa springs. Tibet’s chestnut horse was famed as a divine piebald, while in the northern lands men likewise admired the Quanmaogua. He has examined every soaring steed, from lai to kun; even troubles of bit and peg or injuries beneath the saddle take many changing forms. The twelve imperial stables were famed in former days; when his hand reaches the illness, it vanishes—so wondrously does the cure prove true. The ancients have passed away, yet their names remain undimmed; now in our own age Huangfu Duan appears again. He knows how to cure all four hundred and eight maladies; his twin pupils gleam brightly like pearls rolling upon a tray. Heaven truly intended to gather the loyal and good; Zhang Qing’s recommendation of this eagle was indeed an excellent plan. Liangshan Marsh gains one more man, styled Count Purple Beard, descendant of Bo Le.

p.src: When Song Jiang saw Huangfu Duan, he perceived at once that the man was no ordinary figure: he had blue eyes with double pupils and a curling beard that hung below his belly. Song Jiang praised him without cease. Huangfu Duan, seeing Song Jiang's devotion to honor and fellowship, was greatly pleased and declared himself willing to join their righteous cause. Song Jiang was overjoyed. After speaking words of comfort to him, he issued orders for all the chieftains to make ready the carts and equipment, provisions, gold, and silver, and then the whole company set out together. They transported the money and provisions of the two prefectures back to the stronghold. The commanders of both the vanguard and the rear guard all moved out. Nothing worthy of mention occurred along the way, and before long they were back in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness at Liangshan Marsh. Song Jiang ordered Gong Wang and Ding Desun to be released and likewise soothed them with kindly words. The two men bowed their heads to the ground and surrendered. With Huangfu Duan now added to the stronghold, he was placed in special charge of treating the animals. Dong Ping and Zhang Qing also became chieftains of the stronghold. Delighted, Song Jiang at once ordered a celebratory banquet to be prepared. Everyone assembled in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness and took their seats according to rank. As Song Jiang looked over the assembled chieftains, he found that they numbered exactly one hundred and eight. Song Jiang began to speak: “Brothers, ever since we gathered together on this mountain, we have suffered no mishap wherever we have gone. This has all been through Heaven's protection, not through human power. That I have now been raised up as your chief is entirely owing to the valor of all you brothers. First, it was ordained that we should unite in righteousness; second, I have something more to say, and I ask all you brothers to hear me out.” Wu Yong said, “Brother, pray give us your commands.” Facing all the chieftains, Song Jiang opened his mouth and set forth his plan. And indeed, what followed was this: the Thirty-six Spirits of the Heavenly Firmament descended to transform the earth, while the Seventy-two Fiends of the Earthly Host threw the Central Plain into tumult. But what plan did Song Gongming ultimately propose? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
